recommendation_1: Reduce the hidden dimensions in the fully connected layers from 128 to 32 to drastically decrease the number of trainable parameters and memory footprint.
rationale_1: The current implementation uses 128 hidden units which increases both computational overhead and memory usage. Reducing this to 32 will significantly lower energy consumption and RAM requirements without sacrificing much accuracy based on previous experiments.
recommendation_3: Apply L1 Unstructured Pruning to the linear layers with a pruning amount of 0.4 to remove redundant weights and reduce model size.
rationale_3: Pruning reduces the number of active parameters, leading to lower memory usage and improved energy efficiency. Using L1 unstructured pruning ensures sparsity is maintained post-training through prune.remove() calls.
recommendation_4: Switch to Bfloat16 Autocast for CPU execution using torch.amp.autocast during training and inference phases.
rationale_4: Using bf16 precision reduces memory consumption and accelerates computation on CPUs, especially beneficial when deploying models on edge devices within the Flower framework.
recommendation_5: Replace ReLU activation with SiLU (Swish) activation function to potentially improve convergence speed and reduce energy consumption.
rationale_5: SiLU activation has been shown to outperform ReLU in terms of training efficiency and can lead to better generalization, thus reducing overall training time and associated energy costs.
